question: Explain how the place of supply of goods, other than goods imported into or exported from India, is determined under section 10 of the IGST Act, 2017.

points.label: Supply involving movement of goods
points.description: Where the supply involves movement of goods, whether by the supplier, the recipient or anyone else, the place of supply is where the movement ends for delivery to the recipient.

points.label: Delivery on the direction of a third person
points.description: Where goods are delivered to the recipient or another person on the direction of a third person (bill-to-ship-to), the third person is treated as having received the goods and the place of supply is the principal place of business of that third person.

points.label: No movement of goods
points.description: Where the supply does not involve movement of goods, the place of supply is the location of the goods at the time of delivery to the recipient.

points.label: Goods assembled or installed at site
points.description: Where goods are assembled or installed at site, the place of supply is the place of assembly or installation.

points.label: Goods supplied on board a conveyance and significance
points.description: Where goods are supplied on board a vessel, aircraft, train or motor vehicle, the place of supply is where the goods are taken on board. The place of supply, compared with the supplier's location, decides whether the supply is inter-State (IGST) or intra-State (CGST and SGST).
points.basis: IGST Act, 2017, section 10(1)(e), read with sections 7 and 8
